stages/input: A small ConvNet for color images, thirty two by thirty two. Follow the shape from layer to layer.
stages/conv: A three by three conv with sixteen filters and padding one keeps the size and makes sixteen channels: sixteen by thirty two by thirty two.
stages/relu: A ReLU works entry by entry, so the shape does not change.
stages/pool: Max pooling halves the height and the width: sixteen by sixteen by sixteen. That is one stage.
stages/repeat: Repeat it with thirty two filters: thirty two channels, then pooled to eight by eight. The image gets smaller and deeper as it goes.
head/flatten: Flatten lays all of it out in one vector: thirty two times eight times eight, two thousand and forty eight numbers.
head/fc: A fully connected layer then turns those into ten class scores, exactly like a linear classifier.
count/c1: Now count what it learns. Each of the first convolution's sixteen filters is three by three over the input's three channels: twenty seven weights, plus one bias. Sixteen times twenty eight is four hundred and forty eight.
count/c2: The second convolution's filters each span all sixteen channels coming in: three times three times sixteen, a hundred and forty four weights, plus one bias. Thirty two of them make four thousand, six hundred and forty.
count/lin: The linear layer has a weight for each of the two thousand and forty eight inputs, for each of the ten scores, plus ten biases: twenty thousand, four hundred and ninety.
count/most: Pooling and ReLU have none. In all, twenty five thousand, five hundred and seventy eight, and four fifths of them sit in that last fully connected layer, even in this tiny network.
